examples.ko: 두 나라는 오래전부터 교역을 해 왔어요.
examples.en: The two countries have traded for a long time.
As trade grew, the economy grew.
The port was a center of trade.
The volume of trade is growing every year.

examples.ko: 나라 사이의 교역은 법으로 정해져 있어요.
examples.en: Trade between countries is set by law.
The number of trading partner countries increased.

explain: '무역'이 가장 일상적인 말이고, 교역은 나라나 집단 사이에서 물건을 주고받는 느낌이 강해서 역사나 뉴스에 자주 나와요. '교역량', '교역국', '교역 상대'처럼 붙여 써요. 개인이 물건을 사고파는 일에는 '거래'를 써요.
explain_en: '무역' is the most everyday word; 교역 stresses goods being exchanged between countries or groups and shows up in history and news. It appears in '교역량', '교역국', and '교역 상대'. For individuals buying and selling, use '거래'.

examples.en: We trade rice with that country.
Merchants in the old days traded silk.

examples.ko: 두 나라가 자유롭게 교역할 수 있게 됐어요.
examples.en: The two countries can now trade freely.
More countries trade with one another.
They traded with neighboring countries and shared culture too.
He crossed the sea to trade and became rich.

explain: 나라나 큰 집단끼리 물건을 사고팔 때 쓰고, 보통 '~와/과 교역하다'로 말해요. 일상에서는 '무역하다'가 더 흔하고, 개인 사이에는 '거래하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used when countries or large groups buy and sell goods, usually in the pattern '~와/과 교역하다'. '무역하다' is more common in daily talk, and '거래하다' is for individuals.

examples.en: Yeouido is Korea's representative financial district.

examples.ko: 점심시간이 되면 금융가 식당이 직장인들로 붐벼요.
examples.en: At lunchtime, restaurants in the financial district are packed with office workers.
Wall Street in New York is famous as a global financial district.
There are many banks and securities firms near the financial district.

examples.ko: 저는 금융가 쪽에 있는 회사로 출근해요.
examples.en: I commute to a company in the financial district area.
On weekends the financial district is very quiet.

explain: 은행과 증권사가 모여 있는 거리나 지역, 즉 장소를 가리켜요. 사람들이나 업계 전체를 말할 때는 '금융계'를 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a place, the streets or area where banks and securities firms cluster. For the people or industry as a whole, use '금융계'.

examples.en: A tailored suit is expensive, so I bought a ready-made one.

examples.ko: 기성품은 사이즈가 맞는지 입어 봐야 해요.
examples.en: With ready-made clothes, you have to try them on to check the size.

examples.ko: 이 가구는 기성품이라 바로 가져갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: This furniture is ready-made, so you can take it right away.

examples.ko: 기성품 말고 직접 만든 선물을 주고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to give a handmade gift, not something store-bought.
I found a pretty enough outfit even among ready-made ones.

examples.ko: 기성품이 아니라서 주문하면 한 달쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: It's not ready-made, so an order takes about a month.

explain: 미리 만들어 놓고 파는 물건이라서 주문 제작이나 맞춤과 반대되는 말이에요. 옷은 '기성복'이라고 해요. '기성품을 사다'처럼 쓰고, 맞춤은 '맞춤 제작'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: These are goods made in advance and sold, so it is the opposite of custom-made or tailored. Clothes are called '기성복'. People say '기성품을 사다', and tailor-made is '맞춤 제작'.

examples.en: I decided to become an organ donor.
We kept the donor's name secret.
Thanks to the donor, the patient regained health.
The library sent a thank-you letter to the donor.
The donor brought this book in person.

examples.ko: 기증자는 먼저 건강 검사를 받아야 해요.
examples.en: A donor has to take a health check first.

explain: '기증하다'는 대가 없이 주는 것이고 기증자는 그 사람이에요. 피를 주는 사람은 '헌혈자', 돈을 내는 사람은 '기부자'라고 해서 쓰임이 달라요. 장기, 책, 작품 같은 걸 줄 때 '기증자'를 써요.
explain_en: 기증하다 means giving without payment, and the 기증자 is that giver. A blood donor is a 헌혈자 and a money donor is a 기부자, so the usage differs. 기증자 is used for organs, books, artworks and similar gifts.

examples.en: An anonymous donor gave a scholarship fund.

examples.ko: 할머니는 평생 모은 돈을 학교에 기탁하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother donated the money she saved all her life to the school.
The company decided to donate funds to help neighbors in need.
I'm sorting my books to donate them to the library.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 매년 쌀을 복지관에 기탁해요.
examples.en: This shop donates rice to the welfare center every year.
The donated funds are used for neighbors in need.

explain: 일상에서는 '기부하다'를 더 많이 말하고, 기탁하다는 성금, 장학금, 물품을 어떤 기관이나 단체에 맡겨 쓰게 할 때 뉴스 기사에서 볼 수 있어요. 'A가 B에 C를 기탁하다'처럼 받는 곳을 '~에'로 써요.
explain_en: In daily life people say '기부하다' more, while 기탁하다 appears in news articles when funds, scholarships or goods are entrusted to an organization to be used. The recipient is marked with '~에', as in 'A가 B에 C를 기탁하다'.

examples.en: The government distributes rice to the villagers.
I heard they rationed food during the war.

examples.ko: 영화사가 다음 주에 새 영화를 배급할 거예요.
examples.en: The film company will distribute a new movie next week.
The line where food was handed out was long.

examples.ko: 물을 배급하면 모두 조금씩 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If we ration the water, everyone can get a little.
The company handed out masks to the employees.

explain: '배급하다'는 부족한 물건을 정해진 양만큼 나눠 주는 일이에요. 영화에서는 극장에 작품을 공급하는 일도 '배급'이라고 해요. 일반 선물이나 자료를 나눠 줄 때는 '나눠 주다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 배급하다 means giving out scarce goods in set amounts. In film, supplying a movie to theaters is also called 배급. For ordinary gifts or handouts, 나눠 주다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: Winter supplies were delivered to the soldiers.

examples.ko: 재난 지역에 물과 담요 같은 보급품을 보냈어요.
examples.en: We sent supplies such as water and blankets to the disaster area.
Supplies are handed out at a set time.

examples.ko: 눈길 때문에 보급품 트럭이 늦게 도착했어요.
examples.en: The supply truck arrived late because of the snowy road.
These gloves are supplies I received at the training camp.

examples.ko: 산악 훈련 중 보급품에 손을 대면 벌점을 받아요.
examples.en: If you touch the supplies during mountain training, you get a penalty.

explain: 군대나 재난, 구호 현장에서 나눠 주는 물품이에요. 가게에서 파는 물건이 아니라 지급되는 물건이라 '보급품을 지급하다/받다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 말로 '지급품'도 써요.
explain_en: These are goods issued in the military, disaster or relief settings. They are handed out rather than sold in shops, so you say '보급품을 지급하다/받다'. '지급품' is a similar word.

examples.en: The teacher hands out snacks to the students.
We divided the work fairly, so everyone felt at ease.
We first decided how to share the profit.
I will assign roles to the team members.

examples.ko: 돈을 분배하고 나서 서로 싸우지 않았어요.
examples.en: They did not fight after splitting the money.
While dividing the food, I found one was missing.

explain: 정해진 몫이나 규칙에 따라 나누어 줄 때 써요. '나누다'는 반으로 자르는 것도 되지만 '분배하다'는 사람마다 몫을 정해 준다는 느낌이에요. 일, 돈, 역할 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Use it when handing out portions according to a set share or rule. '나누다' can mean just cutting in half, but '분배하다' feels like deciding each person's share. It pairs well with work, money and roles.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 서울에 분점이 세 곳 있어요.
examples.en: That restaurant has three branches in Seoul.
The main store was far, so I went to a nearby branch.
It was so popular that they opened a branch last year.
I heard the branch owner learned to cook at the main store.
The menu is a little different at each branch.

examples.ko: 우리 동네에도 유명한 빵집 분점이 생겼어요.
examples.en: A branch of a famous bakery opened in our neighborhood too.

explain: 짝말은 '본점'이에요. '지점'은 은행이나 회사에도 쓰지만, '분점'은 식당이나 빵집 같은 가게를 말할 때 어울려요. '분점을 내다', '분점을 차리다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '본점' (main store). '지점' can be used for banks and companies too, but '분점' fits shops like restaurants and bakeries. People say '분점을 내다' or '분점을 차리다' for opening one.

examples.ko: 중고 물건을 사고팔 수 있는 앱이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many apps where you can buy and sell secondhand items.
At the market, merchants buy and sell goods.
You have to be careful when buying and selling stocks.
In the old days, people bought and sold goods with rice.

examples.ko: 친구와 중고 옷을 사고팔다 보니 용돈이 늘었어요.
examples.en: Buying and selling used clothes with my friend increased my pocket money.

examples.ko: 외국에서는 물건을 사고팔 때 그 나라 돈을 써야 해요.
examples.en: When you buy and sell things abroad, you have to use that country's money.

explain: '사다'와 '팔다'가 합쳐진 말이라서 사는 쪽과 파는 쪽을 함께 말할 때 써요. 중고 거래, 주식, 시장 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 한 사람이 사기만 하거나 팔기만 할 때는 '사다'나 '팔다'를 따로 써요.
explain_en: It combines '사다' (buy) and '팔다' (sell), so use it when you talk about both sides of trading. It often appears with secondhand deals, stocks and markets. If someone only buys or only sells, use '사다' or '팔다' alone.

examples.ko: 소매상은 도매상에게서 물건을 사 와서 팔아요.
examples.en: Retailers buy goods from wholesalers and sell them.
My parents run a small retail shop.
Retailers are pushing back against the price increase.
I tend to buy fruit from a local retailer.

examples.ko: 소매상 몇 곳에 전화해서 가격을 비교했어요.
examples.en: I called a few retailers and compared prices.
The wholesaler discussed terms of trade with the retailer.

explain: '도매상'의 반대말로, 물건을 소비자에게 직접 파는 상인이나 가게를 말해요. 가게 자체는 '소매점', 그런 업종은 '소매업'이라고 해서 셋이 짝을 이뤄요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '도매상' and refers to a merchant or shop that sells directly to consumers. The shop itself is '소매점' and the line of business is '소매업', so the three words form a set.

en: operate; manage (funds, systems); apply, put to use (a system)

examples.en: The bank manages its customers' money.

examples.ko: 이 동아리는 적은 회비를 아껴서 운용하고 있어요.
examples.en: This club manages its small membership fees carefully.
You need practice to operate the system well.

examples.ko: 회사가 새 제도를 운용한 지 1년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been a year since the company began running the new system.
How are you going to manage the money you have?
That department operates fifty computer servers.

explain: 돈, 장비, 제도를 목적에 맞게 잘 움직일 때 써요. 가게나 회사를 꾸려 갈 때는 '운영하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 기계를 손으로 직접 다룰 때는 '조작하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it for putting money, equipment, or a system to work toward a goal. For running a shop or company, '운영하다' sounds more natural. For handling a machine by hand, use '조작하다'.

examples.ko: 경제 시간에 재화와 서비스의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In economics class we learned the difference between goods and services.
Rice is a good that people absolutely need.
The price of goods changes depending on demand.

examples.ko: 자원이 부족하면 재화를 나눠 쓰기가 어려워요.
examples.en: When resources are scarce, it's hard to share goods.

examples.ko: 공기는 돈을 내지 않아도 쓰는 재화예요.
examples.en: Air is a good we use without paying.
Each country has a different way of producing goods.

explain: '재화'는 경제에서 사람의 필요를 채우는 물건을 말해요. 책, 쌀, 옷 같은 것이고, 눈에 안 보이는 일은 '서비스'라고 해요. 일상에서는 '물건'이나 '상품'을 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: 재화 is an economics term for things that satisfy human needs, like books, rice, and clothes. Things you can't see, such as work done for you, are 서비스. In daily life 물건 or 상품 is used more.
